title: Cache Priority Tiering — Decision Mapper and Microflow Prototype
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and prototype a decision-mapper UI that lets operators assign workloads to cache priority tiers (Hot, Warm, Cold, Ephemeral) and simulate the impact on latency, token cost, and throughput. The mapper should make trade-offs explicit, include explainers and guardrails, integrate with rollout policies, and support keyboard-first interactions for accessibility.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive prototype in Figma with drag/drop and keyboard controls for moving workloads between tiers
Simulation panel that projects estimated P95 latency and monthly token cost delta for the selected configuration
Microcopy for each tier explaining trade-offs and recommended use-cases (>=3 variants tested)
Guardrail toggles: min-throughput, fallback-model, prefix-preserve option implemented in design
Handoff notes and component spec added to the Console component library with tokens and states
Design review with PM and Eng signed off or comments addressed
design_notes: Decision mapper is inspired by weighted routing UIs but focused on cache semantics (TTL, prefix match, sequence-length distribution)
We surface three primary signals to operators: expected latency (P50/P95), estimated token cost, and cache hit ratio heuristic
Tiers are color-coded with distinct contrast patterns to be color-blind friendly; icons added for 'ephemeral' and 'cold'
Primary interaction model: drag/drop cards representing workload profiles into tier lanes; secondary: keyboard + dropdown assignment
Simulations use historical route-level telemetry (sampled) and per-request length distribution to estimate impact — simulation results are approximations and include confidence bands
Include an 'explainability' flyout showing which requests are likely to be affected and example prompts that would be prefetched or evicted
usability_testing: 03/04/2026 — 5 ops engineers (customer-facing infra teams): median completion time 7m to move 4 workloads and interpret simulation
Findings: novices expected preset recommendations; experts wanted bulk-assign and CSV import
Notable friction: unclear meaning of 'prefix-preserve' toggle — microcopy rewritten to 'Keep prefix-specific cached states across evictions'
Accessibility check: keyboard reorder works but needs ARIA live region when simulation updates — dev ticket created
review_feedback: PM (Noah Patel): add 'Recommended by Redwood' quick-apply state based on workload similarity to known patterns
Eng (Priya Rao): simulation needs a latency margin and a server-side API contract; pointed to telemetry sampling limitations
Security (Avery Martinez): confirm KMS usage required for any persisted workload metadata in Private deployments
Design lead (Maya Chen): simplify tier copy, reduce visual noise in low-contrast dashboards
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: keep simulation client-side for instant feedback; persist config to server only on Save to avoid accidental rollout
Trade-off: showing precise cost numbers would require billing aggregation that delays feedback; we show ranges and an option to 'Run full cost estimate' that triggers a longer server job
Decision: support CSV import for bulk assignments in Phase 2 to reduce initial complexity
Trade-off: supporting per-prefix TTL exposes complexity—expose advanced TTL controls behind an 'Advanced' panel

next_steps: Address Eng review comments and add API contract sketch by 2026-03-15
Add 'Recommended' quick-apply with backlog task and simple heuristic (match on route tags and token distribution)
Prepare handoff doc and tokens, finalize component states, and schedule dev kickoff (2026-03-17)
Phase 2: CSV import, per-prefix TTL, and bulk-simulate for >1000 workloads
notes: Prototype intentionally omits rollout automation; mapping UI will surface 'Save & Apply (canary)' and link to rollout page
Keep educational copy terse — users are primarily infra engineers; include 'Why this matters' inline help targetting PMs
Consider adding a 'what-if' toggle to simulate eviction storm scenarios
